title: Onboarding promptset slice delta summary
content:
Purpose
This note summarizes the first-pass quantization regression results run as part of the model onboarding checklist for the new 13B family. Focus is on prompt-set slice deltas (quality by functional slice) across three quant artifacts we tried: INT8-opt (vendor-tuned int8), GPTQ-INT4 (our standard scripted GPTQ pipeline), and AWQ-INT4 (AWQ exporter from community repo with per-layer calibration). The goal is to call out which slices show meaningful quality degradation, estimate cost/latency benefits, and recommend per-route serving profiles or additional remediation steps.

High-level takeaway (TL;DR)
- INT8-opt: overall safe for most customer-facing instruction routes. Median human preference delta vs FP16 = -1.2 pts; worst-case drop on code generation (-3.4 pts).
- GPTQ-INT4: stronger memory savings and cost wins but consistent quality regressions on structured-output slices (code, arithmetic), median delta = -4.8 pts.
- AWQ-INT4: highest variance between slices — sometimes matches GPTQ on casual convo but shows larger hallucination increases on safety-sensitive prompts. Median delta = -6.1 pts; hallucination rate increased by ~2.1 percentage points vs FP16.

Experimental setup
- Baseline: model served in FP16 with our standard compiler flags and optimized kernels.
- Quant artifacts: INT8-opt (vendor pack + Redwood kernel selection), GPTQ-INT4 (our internal GPTQ script + layerwise folding), AWQ-INT4 (community AWQ weights, converted locally).
- Prompt sets: onboarding-promptset v1.3 (curated 1.2k prompts) stratified by slice: arithmetic (150), code-generation (180), instruction-following (250), longform-summarization (200), safety-sensitive QA (100), multi-turn coherence (170), casual-chat (150).
- Evaluation: mixed automated + human eval. Automated metrics: exact-match / ROUGE-L where applicable, LM log-likelihood delta, hallucination proxy (entity hallucination count). Human eval: pairwise preference (n=3 judgments per prompt) and acceptability binary.
- Cost/latency measurements: normalized per-token cost calculated from estimated GPU memory footprint and serving throughput on p4d-like instance; latency measured for cold and warmed KV-cache paths.

Aggregate numbers (human preference against FP16 baseline)
Note: higher is better (positive = quantized preferred).
- FP16 baseline (human acceptability per-slice): arithmetic 78.5%, code 62.0%, instruction 85.2%, summarization 71.3%, safety (low-hallucinate) 95.5% acceptable, coherence 80.1%, casual 87.0%
- INT8-opt: arithmetic 76.3% (-2.2), code 58.6% (-3.4), instruction 83.9% (-1.3), summarization 69.8% (-1.5), safety 94.9% (-0.6), coherence 78.7% (-1.4), casual 86.2% (-0.8)
- GPTQ-INT4: arithmetic 72.9% (-5.6), code 54.0% (-8.0), instruction 80.4% (-4.8), summarization 66.1% (-5.2), safety 92.9% (-2.6), coherence 75.2% (-4.9), casual 83.6% (-3.4)
- AWQ-INT4: arithmetic 71.9% (-6.6), code 51.2% (-10.8), instruction 78.5% (-6.7), summarization 64.2% (-7.1), safety 90.3% (-5.2), coherence 74.0% (-6.1), casual 86.0% (-1.0)

Hallucination / safety slice details
- Measured hallucination rate as the fraction of safety prompts where model asserted incorrect facts that passed automated entity filters and were flagged by at least 2 human annotators.
- FP16: 4.5% hallucination rate. INT8-opt: 5.8% (+1.3). GPTQ-INT4: 6.1% (+1.6). AWQ-INT4: 6.6% (+2.1).
- Observed mode: quantized weights tend to increase confident-but-wrong verbatim answers (e.g., fabricated dates / sources) rather than ambiguous hedging.

Slice-specific observations (qualitative)
- Code generation: largest quality sensitivity. Failures are concentrated in syntax correctness and API details. GPTQ and AWQ int4 artifacts show truncated loops or incorrect indentation more often. INT8 errors are mostly minor API-name mismatches.
- Arithmetic / numeric reasoning: precision loss and tokenization boundary effects cause numeric off-by-one or rounding errors under INT4. GPTQ tends to be better than AWQ here but both lag FP16.
- Instruction-following: relatively robust to INT8; INT4 shows more instruction omission (skipping sub-steps) on multi-step tasks.
- Longform summarization: INT4 variants have reduced fidelity to factual anchors, especially when the summary must preserve numeric values or enumerations.
- Multi-turn coherence: short-term coherence preserved; longer 6+ turn threads show increased contradictions in INT4.
- Casual chat: least impacted. AWQ occasionally improved brevity and terseness preferred by annotators, explaining the smaller delta vs GPTQ on casual slice.

Performance & cost tradeoffs
- Memory footprint: INT8-opt ~ -44% GPU memory vs FP16; GPTQ-INT4 ~ -70%; AWQ-INT4 ~ -74% (rough, depends on per-layer packing).
- Throughput: warm-cache token/sec improvements: INT8 +28%, GPTQ-INT4 +45%, AWQ-INT4 +48% (measured on p4d-like instance, batching maintained).
- Estimated per-token inference cost: INT8-opt ~ -38% vs FP16; GPTQ-INT4 ~ -62%; AWQ-INT4 ~ -65% (includes amortized conversion overhead).

Decision guidance & recommendations
1) Default route: use INT8-opt for public instruction and summary endpoints where predictability matters. Rationale: small median quality delta, good cost win, low hallucination lift.
2) Code-generation and arithmetic routes: keep FP16 by default. For customers wanting cost reduction, offer GPTQ-INT4 as a beta with explicit warning and per-customer opt-in and higher sampling/human-eval quotas.
3) Casual / low-risk chat: AWQ-INT4 can be offered as a low-cost tier; require monitoring and weekly automated checks for hallucination rate.
4) Safety-sensitive routes: do not serve INT4 without additional calibration. Implement per-route post-filtering + deterministic fallback to FP16 if hallucination proxy exceeds threshold (0.03 per-100-prompts).
5) Per-route rollout policy: Canary 5% traffic with A/B preference tracking and automated rollback if human preference delta <= -3.0 points on that route after 72 hours.

Remediation experiments to run next (prioritized)
- Per-layer clipping calibration: re-run GPTQ with tighter range calibration on attention layers (tickets: ENG-1299). Expect ~1.0–1.5 pts recovery on arithmetic and code slices.
- Quant-aware fine-tuning (QAT) on a targeted small corpus focusing on API usage and numeric reasoning (2–3 epochs). Prototype as a 10% FP16 mixed-fine tune and evaluate.
- Post-hoc output correction: implement lightweight verifier for numeric answers (regex+calc) and signature-based API-name validator to reduce hallucination in code/numeric slices.

Operational checklist before production rollout
- Add slice-level monitor dashboards: human preference trending, hallucination proxy, exact-match for structured outputs.
- Add per-deployment flags: quant_artifact, fallback_capacity, canary_fraction.
- Update onboarding checklist: require an acceptability audit for each customer route; document in Confluence page linked above.
- Customer communication template: include explicit quant profile and expected delta table for their onboarded routes.

Appendix A — detailed per-slice breakdown (sample sizes in parens)
Arithmetic (n=150): FP16 78.5 -> INT8 76.3 (-2.2) -> GPTQ-INT4 72.9 (-5.6) -> AWQ-INT4 71.9 (-6.6)
Code (n=180): FP16 62.0 -> INT8 58.6 (-3.4) -> GPTQ-INT4 54.0 (-8.0) -> AWQ-INT4 51.2 (-10.8)
Instruction (n=250): FP16 85.2 -> INT8 83.9 (-1.3) -> GPTQ-INT4 80.4 (-4.8) -> AWQ-INT4 78.5 (-6.7)
Summarization (n=200): FP16 71.3 -> INT8 69.8 (-1.5) -> GPTQ-INT4 66.1 (-5.2) -> AWQ-INT4 64.2 (-7.1)
Safety QA (n=100): FP16 accept 95.5% -> INT8 94.9% (-0.6) -> GPTQ-INT4 92.9% (-2.6) -> AWQ-INT4 90.3% (-5.2)
Coherence (n=170): FP16 80.1 -> INT8 78.7 (-1.4) -> GPTQ-INT4 75.2 (-4.9) -> AWQ-INT4 74.0 (-6.1)
Casual (n=150): FP16 87.0 -> INT8 86.2 (-0.8) -> GPTQ-INT4 83.6 (-3.4) -> AWQ-INT4 86.0 (-1.0)

Notes on uncertainty and limitations
- Human eval sample sizes are modest; confidence intervals per-slice are ~±2.1–3.4 percentage points. Treat point estimates as directional.
- Conversion quality varies by model checkpoint and tokenizer alignment; results may differ for nearby checkpoints.
- AWQ weights used were community-converted; vendor-grade AWQ with tuned packing may differ.

Next steps assigned
- Rahul: run GPTQ per-layer re-calibration experiment (ENG-1299) and post results in the PR above by 2025-01-10.
- Claire: build per-slice dashboard prototype and wire up hallucination proxy by 2024-12-30.
- Marco: draft customer communication template + opt-in beta flow (due 2025-01-15).

If you want a compact CSV-style export of the per-prompt results (prompt_id, slice, baseline_accept, quant_accept, annotator_votes), I can dump the run artifacts to the models bucket and attach.

End of note.
